literal: Third month: Prince of Hexi Juqu Mujian plotted rebellion and was executed in secret.
idiomatic: In the third month Mujian, Prince of Hexi of the Juqu, plotted rebellion and was secretly executed.

literal: Three thousand Dingzhou Dingling households were moved to the capital.
idiomatic: Three thousand Dingling households of Dingzhou were moved to the capital.

literal: Summer, fifth month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer the court returned to the capital.

literal: Sixth month: the western campaign generals Yuan Chuzhen of Fufeng and eight other generals, for embezzling military supplies and plundering where they were posted, with booty each reckoned in the tens of millions, were all beheaded.
idiomatic: In the sixth month Yuan Chuzhen of Fufeng and eight western generals were beheaded for embezzling supplies and plundering, booty reckoned in tens of millions each.

literal: Eighth month: Grand General of the Guard, Prince of Le'an Fan, died.
idiomatic: In the eighth month Fan, Prince of Le'an, Grand General of the Guard, died.

literal: Year 9, spring, first month: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the ninth year, first month of spring, Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.

literal: The Di Yang Wendé accepted office from Yilong, held Jialu Fort, and drew the Di of the five divisions of Wudu and Yinping.
idiomatic: The Di Yang Wendé took rank from Yilong, held Jialu Fort, and drew the five Di divisions of Wudu and Yinping.

literal: An edict that the Chouchi garrison commander Pi Baozi was to campaign against him; Wendé abandoned the city and fled south; his wife, children, and staff were captured.
idiomatic: He ordered Pi Baozi, Chouchi garrison commander, against him; Wendé fled south and his family and staff were taken.

literal: Yilong's Administrator of Baishui Lang Qixuan led a host to rescue Wendé; Baozi met and greatly defeated him; Qixuan and Wendé fled back to Hanzhong.
idiomatic: Lang Qixuan, Yilong's Administrator of Baishui, came to rescue Wendé; Baozi met and routed him; Qixuan and Wendé fled to Hanzhong.

literal: The Qiang chieftain of Dangchang, Liang Jin'ci, sent envoys to submit inward and also presented local products.
idiomatic: Liang Jin'ci, Qiang chieftain of Dangchang, sent envoys to submit with local tribute.

literal: Second month, day guimao: the imperial carriage traveled to Dingzhou.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the guimao day, the emperor went to Dingzhou.

literal: The people east of the mountains suffered famine; granaries were opened for relief.
idiomatic: The people east of the mountains suffered famine; storehouses were opened.

literal: Work on the frontier encirclement was halted.
idiomatic: Work on the frontier barrier was halted.

literal: He then traveled west to Shangdang, executed more than two thousand rebel households of Lu, and moved more than five thousand households of Lishi in Xihe to the capital.
idiomatic: He went west to Shangdang, executed more than two thousand rebel households of Lu, and moved more than five thousand Lishi households of Xihe to the capital.

literal: An edict piled stone as three mounds on Great King Mountain northeast of Huguan and also cut away the northern foot of Phoenix Mountain to sever it.
idiomatic: He ordered stone piled as three mounds on Great King Mountain northeast of Huguan and the northern foot of Phoenix Mountain cut away.

literal: Third month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the third month the court returned to the capital.

literal: Summer, fifth month, day jiaxu: Duke of Jiaozhi Han Ba was made Acting Commander, General Who Conquers the West, Colonel Protector of the Western Rong, and King of Shanshan, garrisoning Shanshan and levying corvée on its people like a commandery or district.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on the jiaxu day, Han Ba, Duke of Jiaozhi, was made Acting Commander, General Who Conquers the West, Colonel Protector of the Western Rong, and King of Shanshan, garrisoning Shanshan and levying its people like a district.

literal: Sixth month, day xinyou: the imperial carriage traveled to Broad Virtue Palace.
idiomatic: On the xinyou day of the sixth month the emperor went to Broad Virtue Palace.

literal: Day dingmao: the state of Yueban sent envoys asking to campaign against the Rouran together with the royal army; the Emperor granted it.
idiomatic: On the dingmao day Yueban asked to campaign against the Rouran with the royal army; the Emperor granted it.

literal: Autumn, eighth month: an edict that all armies at court and in the provinces were to stand in readiness.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he ordered all armies to stand ready.

literal: Ninth month, day yiyou: troops were arrayed at the western suburb.
idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the ninth month troops were arrayed at the western suburb.

literal: Day bingxu: the Emperor came to Yinshan.
idiomatic: On the bingxu day the Emperor came to Yinshan.

literal: That month Duke of Chenggong Wandu Gui came a thousand li by post-horse relay and greatly defeated the state of Yanqi; its king Jushibina fled to Kucha.
idiomatic: That month Wandu Gui came a thousand li by relay and routed Yanqi; King Jushibina fled to Kucha.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day xinchou: Prince of Hengnong Xi Jin died.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the xinchou day, Xi Jin, Prince of Hengnong, died.

literal: Day guimao: because marriage was extravagant and funerals excessive, an edict ordered the officials to set new regulations and limits.
idiomatic: On the guimao day, because marriage was extravagant and funerals excessive, he ordered new limits set.

literal: Day guihai: a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On the guihai day there was a general amnesty.

literal: Twelfth month: an edict that Duke of Chenggong Wandu Gui was to campaign west from Yanqi against Kucha.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month he ordered Wandu Gui to campaign west from Yanqi against Kucha.

literal: The Crown Prince attended court at the traveling palace, then followed the northern campaign to Shouxiang Fort; no Rouran were seen, so grain was stored in the fort and a garrison left while the army returned.
idiomatic: The Crown Prince attended at the traveling palace, followed the northern campaign to Shouxiang Fort, saw no Rouran, stored grain, left a garrison, and returned.

literal: Prince of Beiping Changsun Dun was reduced to duke for an offense.
idiomatic: Changsun Dun, Prince of Beiping, was reduced to duke for an offense.

literal: Year 10, spring, first month, day wuchen, first day: the Emperor was in the southern desert and feasted the hundred officials, distributing rewards each according to rank.
idiomatic: In the tenth year, on the new-year wuchen day, the Emperor was in the southern desert, feasted the hundred officials, and rewarded each by rank.

literal: Day jiaxu: the northern campaign.
idiomatic: On the jiaxu day the northern campaign began.

literal: Second month: Rouran chieftains Ermitaba and others led more than a thousand households of their tribe to submit; Rouran Tuhezhen fled in fear to a distance.
idiomatic: In the second month Rouran chiefs Ermitaba and others led more than a thousand households to submit; Tuhezhen of the Rouran fled far in fear.

literal: The account is fully set forth in the Rouran treatise.
idiomatic: The full account is in the treatise on the Rouran.

literal: Third month: a hunt was then held in Hexi.
idiomatic: In the third month a hunt was held in Hexi.

literal: Day gengyin: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the gengyin day the court returned to the capital.

literal: Summer, fifth month, day gengyin: the imperial carriage traveled to Yinshan.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on the gengyin day, the emperor went to Yinshan.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: the state of Futusha sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the state of Futusha sent tribute.

literal: Ninth month: arms were reviewed on the desert; then the northern campaign.
idiomatic: In the ninth month arms were reviewed on the desert, then the northern campaign.

literal: The account is fully set forth in the Rouran treatise.
idiomatic: The full account is in the treatise on the Rouran.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day gengzi: the Crown Prince and the host of officials welcomed the Emperor at the traveling palace.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the gengzi day, the Crown Prince and officials welcomed the Emperor at the traveling palace.

literal: Day renwu: a great feast; booty and cloth and silk were distributed, each according to rank.
idiomatic: On the renwu day there was a great feast; booty and cloth were distributed by rank.

literal: Eleventh month: Kucha, Shule, Boluona, and Yuankuo states each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month Kucha, Shule, Boluona, and Yuankuo each sent tribute.

literal: Twelfth month, day wushen: the imperial carriage returned from the northern campaign.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the wushen day, the court returned from the northern campaign.

literal: Day jiyou: Duke of Pingchang Yuan Tuozhen was made Prince of Zhongshan.
idiomatic: On the jiyou day Tuozhen, Duke of Pingchang, was made Prince of Zhongshan.

literal: Year 11, spring, first month, day yiyou: the imperial carriage traveled to Luoyang; in every commandery and state passed through he personally addressed the aged and comforted orphans and the solitary.
idiomatic: In the eleventh year, on the yiyou day of the first month of spring, the emperor went to Luoyang; in every district passed through he addressed the aged and comforted orphans.

literal: Na, Prince of Gaoliang, was made Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: Na, Prince of Gaoliang, was made Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes.

literal: Second month, day jiawu: a great hunt was held at Liangchuan.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the jiawu day, a great hunt was held at Liangchuan.

literal: Prince Zhen died.
idiomatic: Prince Zhen died.

literal: That month palaces were greatly repaired; the Crown Prince dwelt in the Northern Palace.
idiomatic: That month palaces were greatly repaired; the Crown Prince dwelt in the Northern Palace.

literal: The imperial carriage then campaigned against Xuanchi; envoys were further sent to comfort the people beyond the borders, and those who would not submit were executed.
idiomatic: The emperor then marched on Xuanchi; envoys comforted border peoples and the disobedient were killed.

literal: Prince of Yongchang Ren greatly defeated Liu Yilong's generals Liu Tanzhi and Cheng Tianzuo east of the Ru, beheaded Tanzhi, and captured Tianzuo.
idiomatic: Ren routed Liu Tanzhi and Cheng Tianzuo east of the Ru, beheaded Tanzhi, and captured Tianzuo.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day guimao: the imperial carriage returned to the palace; followers and capital clerks of lang rank and above were given captives each according to rank.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the guimao day, the court returned; followers and capital clerks of lang rank and above received captives by rank.

literal: Sixth month, day jihai: Chancellor of State Cui Hao was executed.
idiomatic: On the jihai day of the sixth month Cui Hao, Chancellor of State, was executed.

literal: Day xinchou: a northern tour of Yinshan.
idiomatic: On the xinchou day he toured Yinshan north.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: Yilong sent his General Who Assists the State Xiao Binzhi with sixty thousand men against Jizhou; Inspector Wang Maidé abandoned the province and fled; Binzhi entered the city and sent General Who Pacifies the North Wang Xuanno west against Huatai.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Yilong sent Xiao Binzhi, General Who Assists the State, with sixty thousand against Jizhou; Inspector Wang Maidé fled; Binzhi took the city and sent Wang Xuanno, General Who Pacifies the North, west against Huatai.

literal: An edict that the Fangtou garrison commander, General Who Pacifies the South, Duke of Nankang Du Daojun was to assist in holding Yanzhou.
idiomatic: He ordered Du Daojun, Duke of Nankang, Fangtou garrison commander and General Who Pacifies the South, to assist in holding Yanzhou.

literal: Eighth month, day guihai: a hunt was held in Hexi.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the guihai day, a hunt was held in Hexi.

literal: Day guimao: troops were arrayed at the western suburb.
idiomatic: On the guimao day troops were arrayed at the western suburb.

literal: Ninth month, day xinmao: the imperial carriage campaigned south.
idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the ninth month the emperor marched south.

literal: Day guisi: the Crown Prince campaigned north and encamped in the southern desert; Prince of Wu Yu remained to guard the capital.
idiomatic: On the guisi day the Crown Prince marched north to the southern desert; Yu, Prince of Wu, guarded the capital.

literal: Day gengzi: a partial amnesty for Ding, Ji, and Xiang provinces from death down.
idiomatic: On the gengzi day there was a partial amnesty in Ding, Ji, and Xiang from death downward.

literal: Fifty thousand troops of provinces and commanderies were distributed to the armies.
idiomatic: Fifty thousand provincial troops were assigned to the armies.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day guihai: the imperial carriage halted at Fangtou.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the guihai day, the court halted at Fangtou.

literal: An edict that Palace Attendant Changsun Zhen with five thousand horse was to cross from Shiji Ford to block Xuanno's escape.
idiomatic: He ordered Changsun Zhen, Palace Attendant, with five thousand horse to cross at Shiji Ford to block Xuanno.

literal: Day yichou: the imperial carriage crossed the river; Xuanno was greatly afraid, abandoned the army and fled, and each host scattered; pursuit trampled and beheaded more than ten thousand; weapons piled like hills.
idiomatic: On the yichou day the emperor crossed the river; Xuanno fled in terror, the hosts scattered, pursuit killed more than ten thousand, and weapons piled like hills.

literal: The Emperor then reached Dongping.
idiomatic: The Emperor then reached Dongping.

literal: Xiao Binzhi abandoned Jizhou and withdrew to defend Licheng.
idiomatic: Xiao Binzhi abandoned Jizhou and withdrew to Licheng.

literal: The generals were then ordered to advance by separate routes: General Who Conquers the West Prince of Yongchang Ren from Luoyang toward Shouchun; Minister of Works Changsun Zhen toward Matou; Prince of Chu Jian toward Zhongli; Prince of Gaoliang Na from Qingzhou toward Xiapi.
idiomatic: He ordered separate advances: Ren from Luoyang on Shouchun; Changsun Zhen on Matou; Jian, Prince of Chu, on Zhongli; Na from Qingzhou on Xiapi.

literal: The imperial carriage by the central route, [5] eleventh month, day xinmao: reached Mount Zou; Liu Yilong's Administrator of Lu commandery Cui Xielü led dependent cities to submit.
idiomatic: By the central route, [5] in the eleventh month on the xinmao day he reached Mount Zou; Cui Xielü, Liu Yilong's Administrator of Lu, led dependent cities to submit.

literal: An envoy was sent with the great offering to sacrifice to Confucius.
idiomatic: An envoy sacrificed to Confucius with the great offering.

literal: Day renzi: he halted at Pengcheng, then pressed toward Xuyi.
idiomatic: On the renzi day he halted at Pengcheng, then pressed toward Xuyi.

literal: The state of Yandun presented one lion.
idiomatic: The state of Yandun presented a lion.

literal: Twelfth month, day dingmao: the imperial carriage reached the Huai.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the dingmao day, the court reached the Huai.

literal: An edict to cut reed and rush; tens of thousands of rafts were launched to cross.
idiomatic: He ordered reeds cut; tens of thousands of rafts crossed the river.

literal: Yilong's defending general of Xuyi, Zang Zhi, shut the gates and held firm.
idiomatic: Zang Zhi, Yilong's defender of Xuyi, shut the gates and held.

literal: General Hu Chongzhi and others led twenty thousand men to relieve Xuyi.
idiomatic: Hu Chongzhi and others led twenty thousand to relieve Xuyi.

literal: Prince of Yan Tan greatly defeated them, displayed Chongzhi and the others, and beheaded more than ten thousand; all Huainan submitted.
idiomatic: Tan, Prince of Yan, routed them, displayed Chongzhi and others, beheaded more than ten thousand, and all Huainan submitted.

literal: That month Prince of Yongchang Ren attacked Xuanchi, took it, captured Yilong's defending general Zhao Huai, and sent him to the capital for execution.
idiomatic: That month Ren took Xuanchi, captured Zhao Huai, Yilong's defender, and sent him to the capital for execution.

literal: Passing Dingxiang and west of the Huai, he greatly defeated Liu Yilong's general Liu Kangzu, beheaded him, and also captured the generals Hu Shengzhi and Wang Luohan and sent them to the traveling palace.
idiomatic: Passing Dingxiang and west of the Huai, he routed Liu Kangzu, beheaded him, and captured Hu Shengzhi and Wang Luohan to the traveling palace.

literal: Day guimao: the imperial carriage came to the river; a traveling palace was raised on Mount Guabu.
idiomatic: On the guimao day the court came to the river and raised a traveling palace on Mount Guabu.

literal: Prince of Yongchang Ren from Liyang to west of the river, Prince of Gaoliang Na from Shanyang to Guangling—all armies on the same day came to the river; every city passed looked to the dust and fled; those who submitted were beyond counting.
idiomatic: Ren from Liyang and Na from Shanyang to Guangling—all reached the river the same day; cities fled at the dust; submissions were beyond count.

literal: Day jiashen: Yilong sent envoys offering a hundred oxen, presenting local products, and also asking to send a daughter to the imperial grandson to seek peace.
idiomatic: On the jiashen day Yilong sent envoys with a hundred oxen and local tribute and asked to send a daughter to the imperial grandson for peace.

literal: The Emperor held that peace by marriage was not ritual; he granted peace but not marriage and sent Palace Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Xiahou Ye in reply.
idiomatic: The Emperor held peace by marriage unritual; he granted peace but not marriage and sent Xiahou Ye in reply.

literal: An edict that the imperial grandson write a letter sending horses in exchange.
idiomatic: He ordered the imperial grandson to write sending horses in exchange.

literal: Summer, fifth month, day renyin: a general amnesty.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on the renyin day, there was a general amnesty.

literal: Sixth month, day renxu: the reign title was changed.
idiomatic: On the renxu day of the sixth month the reign title was changed.

literal: The king of Cheshi sent his son to attend court.
idiomatic: The king of Cheshi sent his son to court.

literal: An edict said: "When the penal net is too dense, offenders grow ever more numerous—We are deeply moved by this.
idiomatic: An edict declared: "When the penal net is too dense, offenders multiply—We are deeply moved.

literal: Let the responsible offices examine the statutes and commands and strive for the mean.
idiomatic: Let the offices examine the statutes and strive for the mean.

literal: Whatever else is inconvenient for the people, add or reduce by comparison."
idiomatic: Whatever else burdens the people, add or reduce by comparison."

literal: An edict that Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince You Ya and Secretariat Gentleman Hu Fanghui and others were to revise and fix the law code.
idiomatic: He ordered You Ya, Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, and Hu Fanghui, Secretariat Gentleman, and others to revise the law code.

literal: Prince of Lueyang Jie'er and Na, Prince of Gaoliang, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, were guilty and granted death.
idiomatic: Jie'er, Prince of Lueyang, and Na, Prince of Gaoliang, Equal to the Three Dukes, were guilty and put to death.

literal: Day wuchen: the Crown Prince died.
idiomatic: On the wuchen day the Crown Prince died.

literal: Day renshen: Emperor Jingmu the Crown Prince was buried at Jinling.
idiomatic: On the renshen day the Crown Prince was buried at Jinling as Emperor Jingmu.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day dinghai: the imperial carriage traveled to Yinshan.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the dinghai day, the emperor went to Yinshan.

literal: Clerical staff of the various bureaus was reduced by one-third.
idiomatic: Clerical staff of the bureaus was cut by one-third.

literal: Ninth month, day guisi: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the guisi day, the court returned to the capital.

literal: Year 2, spring, first month, day gengchen, first day: more than five thousand southern submitter households at Zhongshan plotted rebellion; provincial troops punished and pacified them.
idiomatic: In the second year, on the new-year gengchen day, more than five thousand southern submitter households at Zhongshan rebelled; provincial troops pacified them.

literal: Inspector of Jizhou, Prince of Zhangye Juqu Wannian, conspired with submitters and was granted death.
idiomatic: Wannian, Prince of Zhangye, Inspector of Jizhou, conspired with submitters and was put to death.

literal: Third month, day jiayin: the Emperor died at Yong'an Palace at age forty-five.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the jiayin day, the Emperor died at Yong'an Palace at forty-five.
